category.name: Diagrams and software architecture
category.description: Render or edit diagrams (Mermaid, PlantUML, C4), whiteboards and architecture models.

entries.name: Eraser API (DiagramGPT)
entries.free_tier: paid only - API tokens require an active paid team plan
entries.desc_en: Generate diagrams from text prompts (DiagramGPT) and manage Eraser files programmatically via REST API.
entries.notes: No free tier for API access - tokens are only issued to paid teams, not free accounts.

entries.name: IcePanel API
entries.auth_hint: API key based; OpenAPI 3.1 spec published at api.icepanel.io
entries.free_tier: free tier: 10,000 read requests/mo, 1,000 write requests/mo, 5 import/export requests/mo
entries.desc_en: Programmatically create, read, import, and export C4-style architecture landscapes and models via REST API.
entries.notes: Free plan has meaningful monthly request caps; higher volume requires Growth ($40/editor/mo), Scale ($80/editor/mo), or Enterprise plans.

entries.name: Kroki
entries.free_tier: free, no key; public hosted instance at kroki.io sponsored by Exoscale (no SLA)
entries.desc_en: Render 25+ diagram-as-code formats (PlantUML, Mermaid, C4, GraphViz, BPMN, etc.) from text via a free HTTP GET/POST API.
entries.notes: No authentication or signup required; text diagram in, image out; can be self-hosted via Docker for privacy or higher volume.

entries.name: Lucid (Lucidchart) REST API
entries.auth_hint: Authorization: Bearer <api_key> or OAuth 2.0 access token
entries.desc_en: Create, read, search, and manage Lucidchart documents and folders programmatically via REST API.
entries.notes: Requires enabling Developer Tools on the account first; supports both API-key and OAuth 2.0 client-credential flows; exact free-tier API quota not published in docs.

entries.name: Mermaid Chart API
entries.auth_hint: API token from account settings; MCP tools use bearer-style auth
entries.free_tier: unauthenticated MCP validate/render tools are free; saving to a Mermaid Chart account needs a token, check pricing for limits
entries.desc_en: Validate, render, and save Mermaid diagrams via Mermaid Chart's official MCP server using an account API token.
entries.notes: Broad REST API docs are gated behind a Google Form request (contact-to-access); the MCP server (HTTP https://mcp.mermaid.ai/mcp, SSE https://mcp.mermaid.ai/sse) is the practical self-serve agent interface today.

entries.name: Miro REST API
entries.auth_hint: Authorization: Bearer <access_token> (OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow, or OAuth 2.1 for MCP)
entries.free_tier: free plan allows up to 3 editable team boards; MCP server available on all plans including free
entries.desc_en: Create/read boards and items via REST API, or use Miro's official MCP server to search, build, and summarize boards.
entries.notes: REST access tokens expire in 1 hour (refresh token 60 days); MCP server supports OIDC for enterprise data-safety controls.

entries.name: Napkin AI API
entries.free_tier: included on every plan; any account can create a token and call the API, limited by credits
entries.desc_en: Generate diagrams, flowcharts, mind maps, and charts from text via REST API, exporting to SVG, PNG, or PPT.
entries.notes: Credit-based usage; requests fail with a no_credits error once a team's credits are exhausted.

entries.name: PlantUML Server API
entries.free_tier: free, no key; public hosted server at plantuml.com/plantuml
entries.desc_en: Render UML and architecture-as-code diagrams to PNG/SVG/ASCII via a free public HTTP GET API using encoded diagram text.
entries.notes: Extremely widely used for UML/C4/architecture-as-code; no signup; self-hostable via plantuml.war for privacy or rate-limit control. Added because it's a very common agent-callable diagram-as-code service missing from the candidate list.

entries.name: Structurizr
entries.auth_hint: X-Authorization header: apiKey:base64(HMAC-SHA256(apiSecret, digest)) plus Nonce header
entries.free_tier: free tier: workspaces up to 0.5MB; paid plans raise the limit to 5MB
entries.desc_en: Create and update C4-model software architecture diagram workspaces as JSON via a signed HTTPS API.
entries.notes: Uses a nonstandard HMAC signing scheme rather than a plain bearer token; docs recommend using the Structurizr CLI or client libraries (e.g. Structurizr for Java) instead of calling the raw API directly.
